issues.legal_issue: A trustee holding assets under a written trust for beneficiaries’ benefit is assessable to wealth tax on those assets even though the trustee holds them for, rather than legally on behalf of, the beneficiaries.
material_facts: The settlor transferred property to himself as trustee under a written trust deed for the benefit of himself, his wife and their children.
The Department assessed the trustee to wealth tax in respect of the trust property.
The trustee argued that he held the property for the beneficiaries’ benefit, not on their behalf, and therefore was outside the assessment provision.
issues.conclusion: A trustee is assessable to wealth tax under Section 21(1) in respect of trust assets, even if under general trust law the trustee holds them for the beneficiaries’ benefit rather than on their behalf.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(1) of the Wealth Tax Act, 1957 expressly includes trustees, and for its purposes the words “on behalf of” encompass holding property for beneficiaries’ benefit. Although taxing provisions are strictly construed and ambiguity benefits the assessee, clear legislative intent must be given effect; a construction that makes part of the provision otiose should be avoided. The Court distinguished W. O. Holdsworth v. State of U.P., which concerned a provision that did not mention trustees, and relied on the analogous Section 41(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1922 and the decisions in Commissioner of Income-tax v. Puthiya Ponamanichintakam Wakf, Commissioner of Income-tax v. Kokila Devi, Commissioner of Income-tax v. Manila Bharti, and Commissioner of Income-tax v. Managing Trustees, Nagore Durgha. It approved Suhashini Karuri v. Wealth Tax Officer and Trustees of Gordhandas Govindram Family Charity Trust v. Commissioner of Income-tax.

predicates.trust_asset_wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding is an assessment of wealth tax on assets held in trust.
predicates.trustee_holds_under_written_trust: A trustee holds the assets under a written trust instrument.
predicates.assets_held_for_beneficiaries: The trustee holds the assets for the benefit of one or more beneficiaries.

issues.definition: When a wealth-tax assessment concerns trust assets held by a trustee under a written trust for beneficiaries’ benefit, the trustee is assessable to wealth tax.

issues.legal_issue: A trustee is assessable at the maximum rate when the beneficiaries’ shares in the trust property are indeterminate on the relevant assessment dates.
material_facts: On the relevant valuation dates, the settlor and his wife were alive and entitled to maintenance from the trust property and to reside in part of it.
The settlor’s sons had rights to maintenance and education from the trust property.
The trust deed also provided for the children’s benefit, and the beneficiaries’ interests were not confined to fixed, ascertainable shares on the relevant dates.
issues.conclusion: Because the beneficiaries’ shares were indeterminate on the relevant dates, the trustee had to be assessed under Section 21(4) as it then stood, at the maximum rate.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 21(4) of the Wealth Tax Act, 1957, as it stood at the relevant time, a trustee is assessed at the maximum rate where the shares of the beneficiaries are indeterminate. Rights to maintenance, education, or residence from trust property may make those shares indeterminate.

predicates.trust_asset_wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding is an assessment of wealth tax on assets held in trust.
predicates.trustee_holds_under_written_trust: A trustee holds the assets under a written trust instrument.
predicates.beneficiary_shares_indeterminate: The beneficiaries’ shares in the trust property cannot be determined on the relevant assessment dates, including because beneficiaries have rights to support or residence from the property.

issues.definition: When a trustee holds trust assets under a written trust in a wealth-tax assessment and the beneficiaries’ shares are indeterminate, the trustee is assessed at the maximum rate.
